topics.label: Introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the audience and frames complement as an important but complicated subject for the lecture.

topics.label: Overview of complement’s roles and activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the basic stages of complement activation and explains why complement matters to immune defence and clearance.

topics.label: Complement component nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the naming conventions for complement components and the exceptions that make them confusing.

topics.label: C3 activation and its products
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic focuses on C3 as the central point of complement and explains what its cleavage products do.

topics.label: Complement recognition pathways and the activation threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the recognition pathways initiate C3 deposition and how sufficient local activation reaches the threshold for downstream effects.

topics.label: Complement effector functions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how downstream complement activity turns local activation into pathogen clearance or destruction.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and protection of host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activation on the body’s own cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in complement components and regulators to their distinct clinical presentations.

topics.label: Staphylococcal complement evasion and uses of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic uses Staphylococcus aureus to explain complement evasion and follows protein A from that role to its medical and laboratory uses.

topics.label: Lecture close
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture, thanks the audience, and points to the next lecture.
